Miri induction IV dosing at Weeks 0, 4, and 8; miri maintenance SC dosing from Week 12.
For details about TZP dose escalation, see Section 6.1.4.2.
Visits 2 through 15 will be conducted Q4W. During the Maintenance Period, some of the visits will be remote; for details, see the SoA (Section 1.3).
Visit 801 will occur 4 weeks after the last treatment visit or ED.
For definition of the primary endpoints, see Section 3.

The SoA described below should be followed for all participants enrolled in Study AMCD. However, for those participants whose participation in this study is affected by exceptional circumstances, such as pandemics or natural disasters, please refer to Section 10.16 for additional guidance. If clinically warranted, an unscheduled visit may occur per investigator discretion.
Telehealth visits may be by telephone or other technology. Gray-shaded columns in the SoA tables represent telehealth visits.
Procedures for screening (Visit 1) may be conducted over more than 1 day as long as all activities are completed within the allowable visit tolerance.

data.text: The complete physical examination excludes pelvic, rectal, and breast examinations, unless clinically indicated. All remaining physical examinations throughout the study should include a symptom-directed physical evaluation, as well as an examination of the heart, lungs, abdomen, neurological system, thyroid, and visual examination of the skin. See Section 8.2.1. Assess for TB risk factors, and for signs and symptoms of active TB, including exam of peripheral lymph nodes (see Sections 8.2.1 and 8.2.10).

Perform as indicated based on participant status and standard of care. May be performed by a qualified personnel per local regulations. Every symptom-directed examination should also include an examination of the heart, lungs, abdomen, neurological system, thyroid, and visual examination of the skin. At least every third month after screening, assess for TB risk factors, and for signs and symptoms of active TB, including an assessment of peripheral lymph nodes (Sections 8.2.1 and 8.2.10).

data.text: Patients with UC should undergo colorectal cancer surveillance starting at 8 years after disease onset, as they are at higher risk of developing colorectal cancer. This timing allows for optimal prevention and early detection of colorectal cancer or dysplasia. (Rationale for adding history of UC ≥8 years to Inclusion Criterion 4)

data.description: Protocol Amendment (e) electronically signed and approved by Lilly on 04 Nov 2025 GMT.
